correctness.rationale: Properness confines every color class to one part. The open neighborhood of a vertex is exactly the union of all other parts, so a uniquely occurring neighbor color exists exactly when another part contains a singleton color class. Satisfying every part is therefore equivalent to having at least two witnessing parts. Starting from the monochromatic-per-part proper coloring, each missing witness part costs exactly one extra color; a size-two activated part has one optimal split, while a larger part has one split per singled-out vertex. This proves both the chromatic formula and enumeration. Fresh direct-definition enumeration on 70 complete-multipartite types of order at most nine reproduced the minimum and optimal unlabeled count in every case.

value.rationale: Complete multipartite graphs are a canonical dense family for coloring invariants, and the theorem is a natural complete classification rather than an arbitrary slice. It sharpens general bounds to an exact zero/one/two-extra-color transition and classifies every optimum coloring.
residual_risks: An older equivalent theorem may use substantially different unique-neighborhood terminology.
A broader algorithmic result might contain the complete-multipartite formula implicitly without highlighting the family; no such implication was located.

final_claim: For every complete multipartite graph with at least two parts, a proper coloring is conflict-free exactly when at least two parts contain singleton color classes; therefore the exact proper conflict-free chromatic number is the number of parts plus the deficit of singleton parts from two, and all optimum color partitions are counted by the stated product-sum formula.
limitations: Finite simple connected complete multipartite graphs with at least two nonempty parts only; no list or higher-h variant is asserted.
